title: Home Owners with Private Bank Loans Affected by Rise in Interest Rates and Risk of Foreclosures
what_it_is: Home Owners with Private Bank Loans Affected by Rise in Interest Rates and Risk of Foreclosures

sections.label: Home owners on floating mortgages
sections.summary: As of 2Q2022, one in three home owners with outstanding FI mortgages have packages that move with market interest rates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: As of 2Q2022, one out of three home owners with outstanding mortgages from financial institutions (FIs) are on mortgage packages that move in tandem with market interest rates.

sections.label: Low non-performing mortgages and foreclosures
sections.summary: Non-performing FI mortgages are 0.3%, foreclosures fell since 2021 to under 30 units, and MAS stress tests show most households can service mortgages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The proportion of non-performing mortgages among FI loans is low, at 0.3%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The number of foreclosures has, in fact, trended down since 2021 and has remained low at fewer than 30 units so far this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: MAS does not expect widespread foreclosures in the near to medium term and the situation reflects, in part, the measures we have put in place over the years to limit the amount one can borrow to buy property, including our recent further tightening of these limits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Stress tests by MAS suggest that most households should still be able to service their mortgages under scenarios of further interest rate hikes and significant income losses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: A relatively small proportion of highly leveraged households may, however, be more constrained under the stress scenarios.

sections.label: MAS stress tests and debt restructuring
sections.summary: MAS account-level stress tests found most new borrowers can service debt under a 400-basis point rate rise and 10% income cut.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: If you look at it from a bottom-up perspective, MAS' account level stress tests of new borrowers have assessed that most households, in fact, should be able to continue servicing their debt under stress assumptions of even a 400-basis point increase in interest rate and a 10% reduction in income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: So, we have conducted these stress tests based on quite conservative measures: excluding CPF OA, cash and also in stressing in quite higher interest rate increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But as the Minister for National Development had also earlier mentioned, MAS is working very closely with MND to monitor this situation carefully and, for those who are unable to service their loans, we will find ways in which to allow for debt repayment restructuring as well as to look for alternative housing.
